clue.text: Lots of people holding lessons in meeting-places

indicators.note: holding means the first group of letters grips the second one between its own letters

parts.note: races are large groups of people sharing descent, so lots of people
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A big crowd keeps lessons going in places where people meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting-places' looks like halls or venues for conferences; here the meetings are race meetings, held at the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse races are held at race meetings, and the tracks hosting them are the venues of those gatherings.

clue.text: Apparatus for engineer

explanation.surface: Some kit meant for an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig or lighting rig is equipment; to rig something is to fix or arrange it dishonestly, to engineer the result.

clue.text: Humorist ignoring repetitions in song

indicators.note: ignoring repetitions means each doubled letter in the name is written only once

parts.note: Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland, was a humorous writer

explanation.surface: A comic writer sings a tune without the repeated bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring repetitions' takes one R and one L from the doubled RR and LL in CARROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a joyful hymn or song, especially one sung at Christmas.

clue.text: Section of church cautious about some religious books

indicators.note: about means the cautious word goes round the books, enclosing them

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
NT, the New Testament, is a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Part of a church is wary of certain sacred texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CHARY round NT, the usual abbreviation for the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A chantry is a chapel within a church, endowed for priests to sing masses for the founder's soul.

clue.text: Sleeper's position producing stress

explanation.surface: Where someone sleeps leads to strain.
explanation.walkthrough: A railway sleeper is the beam under the track, so its place is under the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway sleeper lies beneath the rails, under the track; to emphasise a word is to draw a stroke beneath it.

clue.text: Tear dropped over back of finger

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word for dropped is wrapped round the letter

parts.note: to shed is to let fall, as trees drop leaves

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of the word finger

explanation.surface: A tear falls onto the back of someone's finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives R, the last letter of 'finger', and 'over' puts SHED round it. 'Tear' looks like a teardrop; it is the verb to rip.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something to bits is to cut or pull it into strips.

clue.text: Sculpture I installed in farm building

indicators.note: installed in means the letter I is set inside the building word

parts.note: a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: An artwork of mine has been put inside a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: A stabile is the static cousin of Calder's mobiles, so 'Sculpture' is fair; 'farm building' tempts BARN, which will not take an I.
explanation.definitionFit: A stabile is a fixed abstract sculpture, the motionless counterpart of a mobile.

clue.text: Curtail this in different parts of speech

definitions.text: Curtail this in different parts of speech

parts.words: Curtail this in different parts of speech
parts.note: a puppy's tail is often docked; cut the last letter off this word and it becomes the verb of doing, a different part of speech from the noun

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the tail letter and you get DO, a verb; the full word is a noun, though it can also be a verb meaning to follow. The pun is on docking an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal often has its tail docked, and losing its final letter turns the noun into a verb.

clue.text: Democrat insisted on reforming rebel

indicators.note: on reforming means the following word is rebuilt, its letters forming a new order

explanation.surface: A US Democrat kept on pushing for reform and became a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reforming' is the anagram signal for the letters of 'insisted'; 'Democrat insisted' reads as a sentence, hiding that D stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident openly opposes the established political order, as a rebel does.

clue.text: Conditions for racing stable forming strong partnership

parts.note: in horse racing the going is the state of the ground, the track conditions
steady means stable, firm

explanation.surface: Track conditions for a racing stable are building a strong alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horses' stable alongside racing, but it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a settled romantic relationship are said to be dating regularly and exclusively, building a lasting bond.

clue.text: Foreigner with appropriate article found in plant

parts.note: a German is a foreigner to an English speaker
der is the German definite article, the article suited to a German

explanation.surface: An outsider carrying the right item turns up in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'appropriate article' is one fit for a German: DER, German for 'the'. 'plant' looks like a factory; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb of the mint family, genus Teucrium.

clue.text: For a conductor, very limited attack

indicators.note: limited means the attack word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader gets an attack that is very restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' docks the last letter, L, from ASSAIL. 'attack' is a musical term too, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian tempo marking meaning 'very', as in allegro assai, read by musicians and those who lead them.

clue.text: Composer preceding monarch put gun away

indicators.note: preceding means the composer's name comes before the monarch's letters

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed The Planets
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A composer goes before the sovereign, and a weapon is stowed.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen. Read the answer as a verb: to sheathe a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: To holster a pistol is to slip it into its holder, stowing the weapon.

clue.text: Having difficulty without piano, choir's changed instrument

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the difficulty word wraps round the rest

parts.note: hard means difficult, as in having a hard time
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: changed means the letters of choir's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling without a piano, the choir has to switch instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, and 'changed' rearranges the letters of choir's, its S included.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpsichord is a keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked by quills.

clue.text: Dynamic Russian's first in aquatic event

indicators.note: in means the Russian's first letter sits inside the aquatic event

parts.note: diving is a pool event at a swimming gala or the Olympics

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A forceful Russian leads off in the diving competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives R and 'in' puts it into DIVING after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving force is an energetic, forceful one, pushing things forward.

clue.text: Unsafe run I got with hit in the air

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
to sky a ball is to hit it high in the air

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores a run and then skies a dangerous shot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skied shot is hit high and can be caught, so the surface itself is perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous carries danger or the chance of loss.

clue.text: Novelist setting a book inside ancient Asian city

indicators.note: inside means the article and the book are placed within the novelist's name

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A writer sets a book within the ancient city of Central Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting ... inside' is the container signal; 'book' is a book of the Bible, the Gospel of St Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand in Uzbekistan is one of the oldest cities of Central Asia, a Silk Road hub.

clue.text: Burning pope is not fair

parts.note: a fire that is in is still alight, burning
Clement is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: A pope burnt at the stake would say that is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' looks like 'unjust' but describes weather: stormy, cold, wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is harsh and stormy, the opposite of fine weather.

clue.text: Heroine having disaster in pectoral area

indicators.note: disaster in means the letters are thrown into chaos and rearranged

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area, as in maths

explanation.surface: A heroine suffers a calamity in the chest region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster in' is the anagram signal, and A is the usual abbreviation for area. The surface recalls the Egyptian queen dying from an asp's bite at her breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen is the title heroine of Shakespeare's tragedy Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Amount of money last reported in unspecified location

indicators.note: reported means the words are spoken, so the answer sounds like them

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money, and to wear is to last or endure

explanation.surface: A sum of money was last reported somewhere unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that SUM plus WEAR, said aloud, gives the answer. 'last' is the verb to endure, not 'most recent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb refers to some place not named or known.

clue.text: Party official understood something that cuts both ways

parts.note: a whip is the party official who keeps MPs voting in line
saw means understood, as in 'I saw what you meant'

explanation.surface: A party enforcer understood that a policy could backfire.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip is the British party official who makes members vote as told. 'cuts both ways' sounds like a double-edged argument; it is a saw used on the push and the pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipsaw is a long two-handled saw that cuts on both the forward and back strokes.

clue.text: Put over the top on Catholic, primarily, a priestly garment

indicators.note: on means the excessive letters are placed after the Catholic's letter
primarily means only the opening letter of Catholic is used

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes it, putting a Catholic first in a church vestment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives C; 'on' places OTT after it, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: In company, plays outlandish song

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit within the company abbreviation
outlandish means bizarre, so the letters of plays are scrambled

explanation.surface: A theatre company stages a bizarre musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' scrambles the letters of 'plays', and 'In' puts them within the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian song style, often topical and witty.

clue.text: Capital that can get you diamond, say, fine in condition

parts.note: a diamond is an example of a playing card

indicators.note: in means the fine letter is put inside the condition word

parts.note: if introduces a condition
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencils

explanation.surface: A city where a diamond could be yours if in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff is the capital of Wales. 'fine in condition' puts F inside IF to make IFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital city is the seat of government in Wales.

clue.text: Just over a pound for gift

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word for just wraps round the pound letter

parts.note: fair means just, equitable
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A present worth a little more than one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just over' looks like 'slightly more than'; 'Just' is FAIR, and it goes over (round) L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair for something is a natural talent, a gift for it.

clue.text: Player's wrong about female horse suiting lady

indicators.note: about means the scrambled player letters go round the female letter
wrong means the letters of player are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A gambler is mistaken about a mare fit for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PLAYER into PALREY, and 'about' puts it round F.
explanation.definitionFit: A palfrey was a gentle riding horse, especially one kept for ladies in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Found among kashmiris, Hindu sage

indicators.note: found among means the letters lie within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A Hindu wise man is found living among Kashmiris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found among' points to kashmiRIS HIndu. 'Hindu' feels like part of the definition but is needed for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu seer or holy poet, a wise man.

clue.text: Authorises love-letters being read out

indicators.note: being read out means the letters are spoken and the answer is their sound

parts.note: love is O, as in tennis, and the letters are Ks, so together O and Ks

explanation.surface: Someone approves love letters that are read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-letters' is not romantic post: love is O, and the letters are Ks, and said aloud they are 'oh-kays'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the go-ahead is to approve or sanction their plan.

clue.text: Transformed tapas into another appetiser

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of tapas into are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Spanish snacks are turned into a different starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' works because tapas are themselves appetisers.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is an Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables served before the main meal.

clue.text: In opening parts of operation, he met some resistance

indicators.note: opening parts of means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: At the start of an operation, a surgeon met some opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some resistance' is a unit of electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit for electrical resistance.

clue.text: One in a thousand, in total, was satisfactory

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes between the two letters making a thousand

parts.note: D is Roman 500, so two Ds make a thousand in total
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being one in a thousand overall was good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, so DD totals a thousand; the second 'in' puts I between them.
explanation.definitionFit: If something served its purpose, it sufficed, as in 'that'll do'.

clue.text: Labour fanatic's obsessive behaviour

parts.note: the fanatic is not a political Labour Party zealot but someone addicted to toil, and this is the compulsion they show

explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like Britain's Labour Party; it means plain work.
explanation.definitionFit: The compulsion to toil constantly is the addiction shown by someone hooked on their job.
